what_its_for: Nabumetone is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis (wear-and-tear arthritis) and rheumatoid arthritis. It belongs to a group of medicines called NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) that help reduce inflammation and pain in your joints.
how_to_take: Take nabumetone by mouth, with or without food. Taking it with food or milk may help if it upsets your stomach. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Do not lie down for at least 10 minutes after taking it. Take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush or chew the tablets.
dosing: The usual adult starting dose is 1000 mg (one tablet) taken once a day, usually at bedtime. Your doctor may increase your dose to 1500 mg or 2000 mg per day if needed, which may be taken as a single dose or split into two doses. Always take only the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more than 2000 mg in one day unless your doctor tells you to.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one, as this can increase your risk of side effects.
storage: Store nabumetone at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use it after the expiration date printed on the label. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely through a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking nabumetone, as it increases your risk of stomach bleeding. Do not take aspirin or other NSAIDs (such as ibuprofen or naproxen) at the same time unless your doctor says it is okay. Avoid smoking, as it can make stomach problems worse. Be careful with activities that require alertness if you feel dizzy. Avoid prolonged sun exposure, as nabumetone may make your skin more sensitive to sunlight. Do not take nabumetone if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you notice: black, tarry, or bloody stools; vomit that looks like coffee grounds; severe stomach pain; chest pain or shortness of breath; sudden vision changes; slurred speech or weakness on one side of your body (signs of a stroke); swelling of the face, lips, throat, or tongue; skin rash, blistering, or peeling; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual weight gain or swelling in your legs or feet; decreased urination; or if your pain suddenly gets much worse. Also call your doctor if you develop high blood pressure, ringing in the ears, or if your symptoms do not improve after a few weeks.
when_it_works: You may start to feel some pain relief within a few days of starting nabumetone, but it may take 1 to 2 weeks to feel the full benefit for joint pain and stiffness. For inflammation reduction, it may take up to 2 to 4 weeks of regular use. Keep taking it as prescribed even if you do not notice immediate improvement.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and older) are at higher risk for stomach bleeding and kidney problems with this medicine and should use the lowest effective dose with careful monitoring. Nabumetone should NOT be used during the last 3 months of pregnancy (third trimester) as it can harm the unborn baby. Talk to your doctor before using it during early pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Use with caution if you have kidney disease, liver disease, heart disease, or high blood pressure, as your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. This medicine is generally not recommended for children.
